current.text: Harris signed with the San Antonio Spurs. He takes Harrison Barnes's place in the rotation.
He is projected to start at power forward next to Fox, Castle, Vassell and Wembanyama.
The Spurs are very deep at forward and on the wing, so his minutes have real competition. A consolidation trade is expected in the relatively near future, but not right now.
His rim finishing fell from 68 to 58 percent last season.
His rim finishing might bounce back in the Spurs offense.
Experts see him as a late pick with limited upside who should return value around picks 140 to 165. One expert would rather wait until round 14, and another says he is not worth a round 10 pick.
He is not an upside flyer. Draft him late only if you need a steady 16 point, 5 rebound forward.
His ESPN rank of 94 is too high because the Spurs are deep.

durable.text: He is a very good defensive rebounder for a power forward.
He is a strong isolation and post scorer who can create a shot when the offense stalls.
He is a streaky three-point shooter, but defenses still have to respect his shot.

note: Harris sits right at the edge of our 144-player draft. His Yahoo rank is 151, experts put him around picks 140 to 165, and he cost 1 USD in our league last year, so he is at most a 1 USD final-round filler. He has no weak category and gives small help in FT% and TO, so he fits any build, but his upside is low. Early in the season, check that he keeps the starting power forward spot and plays about 28 minutes or more in a deep Spurs rotation. If not, he belongs on waivers.
